name: Historic Town Centre (Dorp Street and Die Braak)
tagline: Oak-lined heart of Cape Dutch charm
description: The walkable historic core wraps around Dorp Street and the Die Braak green, with whitewashed gabled buildings, museums, cafes and estate wine bars. It is the most atmospheric base, putting food, coffee and heritage right on your doorstep.
bestFor: Nomads wanting walkability, cafes, heritage and the liveliest central atmosphere
cons: Can be busy and noisy in term time

name: University Quarter
description: Clustered around Stellenbosch University, this youthful quarter is full of student housing, budget eateries, bars and coworking-friendly cafes. Term time buzzes with energy and it offers the town's most affordable rooms, though it quietens noticeably during university holidays.
bestFor: Budget-minded, sociable nomads who enjoy student energy and cheap eats
pros: Walking distance to centre and cafes

name: Die Boord and Brandwacht
description: South and west of the centre, Die Boord and Brandwacht are calm, leafy residential suburbs with houses, apartments and a handy shopping centre. They suit nomads wanting space, quiet and comfort within a short drive or cycle of town.
bestFor: Nomads wanting quiet, comfortable longer-stay homes with easy amenities nearby

name: Wine-Estate Outskirts (Jonkershoek and Devon Valley)
description: On the edges toward Jonkershoek and Devon Valley, you swap streets for vineyards, mountains and wine estates. Guesthouses, cottages and estate stays offer stunning scenery and trail access, ideal for those craving nature and quiet over walkable town life.
bestFor: Outdoor lovers seeking vineyard views, hiking access and peaceful natural surroundings
pros: Direct access to trails and estates
